articles.title: Taiwan passes defence budget after record delay, retains drone funding
articles.excerpt:
Taiwan’s opposition-controlled parliament has approved the government’s annual budget, preserving funding for a drone programme central to the island’s defence plans against China.

Lawmakers passed t...
articles.body_text:
Taiwan’s opposition-controlled parliament has approved the government’s annual budget, preserving funding for a drone programme central to the island’s defence plans against China.

Lawmakers passed the $93bn budget late on Friday, after a record 266 days of political deadlock and its legal deadline, as President William Lai Ching-te’s administration, which lost its parliamentary majority in 2024, continues to clash with opposition parties over government spending.

The approved funding was earmarked for drone development, despite an earlier threat by the main opposition party, the Kuomintang, to slash that funding by 70 percent.

The Kuomintang dropped the proposed cut after concluding there was no wasteful overlap between the development and procurement programmes it had initially cited as justification.

Other reductions included a 60 percent cut to special allowances for government agency heads, a 2.5 percent cut to military equipment and facilities spending, and a 50 percent cut to media policy and publicity budgets.

Before Friday’s vote, the government had been operating under a provisional budget mechanism to keep paying civil servants and funding welfare programmes.

Legislative Speaker Han Kuo-yu, following the vote, said the prolonged delay had caused “social division and a constitutional impasse”.

He called on both the ruling and opposition camps to seek greater compromise going forward.

Lai said in a statement that parliamentary oversight and review of the budget are an important constitutional duty.

In May, the same opposition-controlled legislature cut a proposed $40bn special defence budget by 38 percent, stripping out all funding for domestically produced combat drones and leaving only United States arms purchases intact.

Taiwan’s military currently holds fewer than 5,000 drones, while China is reported to have ordered close to a million for delivery this year, part of a broader regional buildup that includes Ukraine’s target of seven million drones in 2026.

Beijing claims self-ruled Taiwan as its own territory and has sharply escalated military pressure on the island in recent years.

articles.title: Wisconsin Democratic candidate says her party 'left behind' rural America
articles.excerpt:
Blue Dog Democrat Rebecca Cooke spoke about how the party needs to rebuild its relationship with rural and working-class voters that the party had "left behind" in recent years.

Blue Dog Democrat Reb...
articles.body_text:
Blue Dog Democrat Rebecca Cooke spoke about how the party needs to rebuild its relationship with rural and working-class voters that the party had "left behind" in recent years.

Blue Dog Democrat Rebecca Cooke, a Wisconsin congressional candidate, discussed in an interview Thursday how she is trying to set things right after she accused her party of abandoning rural and working-class voters in recent years.

She appeared on the "Politics War Room" podcast with co-hosts James Carville and Al Hunt, known for calling out the far left of the Democratic Party.

"I don’t wanna put you in a box, but you say you’re a Blue Dog and a New Democrat, tell me what it means to be a Blue Dog Democrat," Hunt asked.

"They are folks that are fiscally conservative, socially liberal, are really working from, like, a place-based perspective," Cooke said. "They're people that understand rural Democrats, working-class Democrats, that are showing up in rural communities and working-class spaces that historically our party has left behind. And that's like I think why I was connected with them originally or why I — you know what they were doing resonated with me so much."

JAMES CARVILLE PREDICTS 2028 DEMOCRATIC PRIMARY WILL TEST TRUE STRENGTH OF PARTY'S SOCIALIST WING

Rebecca Cooke talked about her working-class origins and her work as a waitress, suggesting that doing such jobs gives people like her more of a connection with Americans' real kitchen table issues than many other politicians. (Kayla Wolf/Getty Images)

She cited multiple examples of other moderate Democrats who "understand how to talk to people in rural America where I feel like a lot of folks in the Democratic Party don't anymore, and I certainly do."

"I think we've built strong coalitions across this district with farmers, you know, healthcare workers, people in rural communities that feel really left behind," Cooke added.

Hunt cited her past comments, "You've said that in Congress, Republicans are too right-wing and congressional Democrats are too left-wing. Specifically, how has Hakeem Jeffries [been] too left-wing?"

"I'm talking just, I think, in general when I talk — I did an ad last cycle where I was standing in the middle of the road on my parents' farm talking about how folks in DC are either too far left or too far right, and we need more people in the middle that want to work across the aisle to get things done," she said. "I'm somebody that wants to work in a really bipartisan way and not put, you know, party before people or politics before people, and I think that's I think what's important."

Cooke suggested that the Democratic Party needs more candidates from a working-class background, citing her own experience.

"I've been a waitress since I was 16 years old," she said. "I've run a small business here in my community but I also waitress to make ends meet. I did some fellowships last year also, with the group called Third Way, around, you know, how do we get more working-class folks to run for office? How do we connect more with working-class voters in general?"

"And I'm proud of that work because I think there's this disconnect in the party and when we run working-class people, folks come out to vote because people trust those people, right? Folks trust me because I have some of the same lived experience that they they've had, right?," Cooke added.

HAKEEM JEFFRIES DOUBLES DOWN ON 'MAXIMUM WARFARE' RHETORIC, TELLS CRITICS 'I DON'T GIVE A DAMN'

Cooke's campaign noted a recent statement from her that if she sees somebody in a MAGA hat, she’s going to shake their hand and introduce herself . (Brett Carlsen/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

She cited other examples from her life, saying many politicians cannot relate to such experiences.

"We've had to sell our cows because of the low price of milk," Cooke said. "I've had to struggle to compete with the Amazons of the world in running a small business. I know what it's like to sign the front of a paycheck as well as the back of a paycheck, right? And I know what it's like to do hourly wage work. There's a lot of members of Congress that have never done those sorts of things. So when they're making policy that's impacting working families, they're out of touch with that."

Fox News Digital reached out to Cooke's campaign, asking what specific issues she would push for the Democratic Party to moderate on to win back rural and working-class voters.

"Rebecca grew up on a dairy farm and has been campaigning in every county, rural and urban, in the 3rd district because she wants to earn support from Wisconsinites of all backgrounds, including Republicans and Trump supporters," a spokesperson said. "

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Rebecca Cooke grew up on a farm and suggested that experiences like that have made her more politically aware of everyday kitchen table issues than most other politicians. (iStock)

"On MSNOW this week, she said if she sees someone with a MAGA hat, she’s going to shake their hand and introduce herself," the spokesperson continued. "She’s running to fight for working people and has no problem disagreeing with other Democrats, like when she said she’d ‘stand up to Democrats to fight for a secure border,’ she ‘support[s] funding the police fully, and doesn’t believe in universal student loan forgiveness because it only sticks a bandaid on a structural problem.’"

Alexander Hall is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to Alexander.hall@fox.com.

articles.title: California teen faces prison after viral video shows him squaring up, repeatedly kicking sea lion in the face
articles.excerpt:
Tyler Muehl, 18, was captured on video attacking the mammal in San Diego. (KTTV)

A California teenager pleaded guilty Friday to repeatedly kicking a sea lion in the face and chasing the animal as it ...
articles.body_text:
Tyler Muehl, 18, was captured on video attacking the mammal in San Diego. (KTTV)

A California teenager pleaded guilty Friday to repeatedly kicking a sea lion in the face and chasing the animal as it tried to escape, according to video of the attack.

Tyler Muehl, 18, who lives in the San Diego seaside neighborhood of La Jolla, entered his plea in a federal courtroom to a misdemeanor violation of the Marine Mammal Protection Act’s prohibition on harassing wildlife, the Justice Department said.

"Federal crime. Federal consequences," U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon wrote in a statement.

SUSPECT IN VIRAL MONK SEAL HARASSMENT VIDEO SAYS HE WAS DOXXED AS FEDERAL COURT FIGHT BEGINS

Tyler Muehl, 18, repeatedly kicked a sea lion in the face before chasing the animal in San Diego, the Justice Department said. (KTTV)

The incident was investigated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). Muehl admitted to kicking the sea lion on July 22, as the mammal was peacefully sitting on a seawall, federal prosecutors said.

"Intentionally striking or kicking a marine mammal is not only illegal — it is dangerous for the well-being of the animal," said NOAA official Eric Morgan.

The teen approached the animal with his hands squared up, as if he were preparing to fight, authorities said. As he made his approach, Muehl referred to himself as Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) fighter Max Holloway.

He then kicked the animal four times, "which caused the sea lion to rear, flinch, and immediately recoil," prosecutors said.

EL-SAYED IN THE HOT SEAT AFTER 'SICKENING' ANIMAL CONTROL RECORD GOES VIRAL ON SOCIAL MEDIA

Tyler Muehl, 18, seen attacking a sea lion in San Diego on July 22. He pleaded guilty on Friday to violating the Marine Mammal Protection Act’s prohibition on harassment of wildlife. (KTTV)

"After the second kick, the sea lion turned and tried to flee, but Muehl chased after the animal and kicked at it a third time," a DOJ news release states. "As the sea lion tried to get away, it stumbled on the sea wall as it fled."

Officials said the teen kicked the sea lion again and chased it until the animal made its escape.

As part of his plea agreement, Muehl said the video, which went viral online, was a "fair and accurate recording of what occurred."

People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) commented on the incident on its social media accounts.

"Assault is ASSAULT, no matter the species," the group wrote on X in a July 24 post. "Leave animals ALONE, and always speak up when you witness abuse."

Tyler Muehl seen in video footage attacking a sea lion on July 22 in San Diego. (KTTV)

Muehl faces up to one year in prison and $100,000 in fines. He is expected to be sentenced on Oct. 20.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Muehl's attorney for comment.

Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

articles.title: Delta flight diverted twice after lavatory leak floods cabin, leaves passengers stranded for hours
articles.excerpt:
A routine maintenance test flight over northwest England drew widespread attention after its flight path appeared to spell out "I'm bored" on the Flightradar24 flight-tracking website.

A Delta Air Li...
articles.body_text:
A routine maintenance test flight over northwest England drew widespread attention after its flight path appeared to spell out "I'm bored" on the Flightradar24 flight-tracking website.

A Delta Air Lines flight traveling from Paris to Seattle was forced to make an unexpected stop in London after the crew reported a mechanical issue involving an onboard lavatory, the airline said.

Delta Flight 81 departed Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport on Aug. 13 bound for Seattle-Tacoma International Airport when the issue prompted the flight crew to divert to London Heathrow Airport.

The Airbus A330-900 was carrying 209 passengers and 13 crew members at the time, according to information provided by Delta.

As the aircraft approached Heathrow, the flight crew declared an emergency with air traffic control because the plane would be making an overweight landing, the airline said.

FLAMES SHOOT FROM AMERICAN AIRLINES FLIGHT BEFORE EMERGENCY LANDING

A Delta Air Lines aircraft taxis at London Heathrow Airport in London on Oct. 7, 2016. Delta Flight 81 diverted to Heathrow after its crew reported a mechanical issue involving an onboard lavatory. (Simon Dawson/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Despite the emergency declaration, the aircraft landed normally and safely at Heathrow.

Delta maintenance personnel then serviced the Airbus in London in an effort to address the lavatory-related mechanical issue.

"We apologize to our customers for their experience and delay on Delta Flight 81 from Paris-Charles de Gaulle to Seattle, which diverted to London Heathrow after the crew reported a mechanical issue involving an onboard lavatory," a Delta spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"This is not the experience we strive to provide, and we're focused on getting our customers to their destinations as quickly and safely as possible."

LIVE BULLET FOUND ABOARD UNITED FLIGHT FORCES PASSENGERS OFF PLANE FOR SECURITY SWEEP AT DENVER AIRPORT

A Delta Air Lines Airbus A330-900, registration N812NW, is pictured at Leonardo da Vinci–Fiumicino Airport in Italy on July 8, 2025. Delta Flight 81 was operated by an Airbus A330-900 carrying 209 passengers and 13 crew members when it diverted to London. (Massimo Insabato/Archivio Massimo Insabato/Mondadori Portfolio via Getty Images)

Once maintenance work was completed, the aircraft was able to depart Heathrow — but the disruption meant passengers still faced an additional detour before reaching their intended destination on the West Coast.

Instead of continuing directly from London to Seattle, the flight headed to New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport because of the crew's available duty time, according to Delta.

Passengers cleared U.S. Customs at JFK before continuing their journey to Seattle.

The unusual itinerary ultimately took the 209 passengers from Paris to London, then across the Atlantic to New York before they could continue on to Seattle.

Passengers prepare to board a flight at London Heathrow Airport on June 27, 2026. Delta Flight 81 made an unscheduled stop at Heathrow while traveling from Paris to Seattle after its crew reported a mechanical issue. (Marc Fernandes/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Delta did not provide additional details about the specific mechanical problem involving the lavatory or what maintenance was required to address it.

Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

articles.title: Reagan National Airport makes drastic change following deadly 2025 midair collision
articles.excerpt:
FOX Business correspondent Grady Trimble has the latest on the new radar system on 'America Reports.'

A new radar system has been installed at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in the Washing...
articles.body_text:
FOX Business correspondent Grady Trimble has the latest on the new radar system on 'America Reports.'

A new radar system has been installed at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in the Washington, D.C., area following a 2025 midair collision that killed 67 people due to multiple systemic failures.

The airport has received the Surface Movement Radar, known as SMR-4, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Friday. The technology will help air traffic controllers identify aircraft and vehicles moving along runways and taxiways, even in bad weather and low-visibility conditions.

"This new radar is our latest reinforcement tool to equip our controllers as they safeguard our air travel. We’re working at the Speed of Trump to deliver the world-class air traffic control system America deserves," Duffy said.

AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL AUDIO CAPTURES TENSE MOMENT TWO PLANES NEARLY COLLIDED AT BOSTON LOGAN AIRPORT

A new Surface Movement Radar Model 4 (SMR-4) has been installed at the Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA), which came more than a year after a deadly midair collision that killed 67 people. (Department of Transportation)

He said the new radar system will give air traffic controllers a "clearer portrait" of airport activity.

Reagan Airport is the fifth airport to receive the system. Newark Liberty International Airport received the technology earlier this week.

Over the next three years, $30.5 million will be invested in safety and technology upgrades at Reagan National, the Transportation Department said.

The new upgrades came after the Jan. 29, 2025, midair collision between American Airlines Flight 5342, a regional jet operated by PSA Airlines, and a U.S. Army Black Hawk helicopter over the Potomac River near the airport.

FAA INVESTIGATES SOUTHWEST NEAR MISS AFTER AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL SENDS JETS ON COLLISION COURSE

Rescuers on a boat work next to the wreckage of a Black Hawk helicopter at the site of the crash after it collided with the American Eagle flight 5342 which was approaching Reagan Washington National Airport and crashed into the Potomac River, outside Washington, U.S., January 30, 2025. (Kevin Lamarque/Reuters)

All 64 people on the American Eagle flight and three aboard the military helicopter were killed.

The federal government admitted liability for the deadly collision. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said systemic failures in airspace design, safety oversight, and risk management by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the Army contributed to what happened.

"This complex and comprehensive one-year investigation identified serious and long-standing safety gaps in the airspace over our nation’s capital," said Jennifer Homendy, chairwoman of the NTSB, in a January 2026 report. "Sadly, the conditions for this tragedy were in place long before the night of Jan. 29."

Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

articles.title: Lebanon’s PM urges timetable for Israeli withdrawal as Hezbollah slams deal
articles.excerpt: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam is pushing for a clear timetable for Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanese territory, as Hezbollah’s leader accuses Lebanon’s government of exposing the country’s own a...
articles.body_text:
Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam is pushing for a clear timetable for Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanese territory, as Hezbollah’s leader accuses Lebanon’s government of exposing the country’s own army to disgrace by pursuing the deal at all.

According to a statement released by the prime minister’s office on Friday, Salam met United States ambassador to Beirut Michel Issa and General Joseph Clearfield, who heads the US military coordination group for Lebanon, to discuss the military track of the negotiation framework with Israel, along with the latest developments in southern Lebanon.

“Salam stressed the need for Israel to stop destruction operations, expand the scope of pilot areas, and set a clear timetable for Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory,” the statement said.

Lebanon’s Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri met the same US officials separately.

“Israel has not stopped its violations and attacks on Lebanon,” he said, citing continued village demolitions, bulldozed farmland, forest fires and damage to heritage sites.

“The key to stability remains forcing Israel to stop its war and withdraw to the international border.”

Issa called the talks “positive” and said negotiations would continue, without giving a date for the next round.

Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem hit back on Beirut’s remarks, accusing Lebanese officials of putting the army under “undue pressure” by implementing a non-functional agreement.

“How can you accept this ongoing humiliation of the Lebanese army, exposing it to bombardment and Israeli pressures, instead of acting as its protectors?” Qassem said on Friday.

He accused Israel of trying to bind Lebanon to an oversight body controlling the army’s deployment and internal operations.

Qassem pointed out that Israel has kept striking homes and demolishing tunnels inside Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh, the first designated pilot zone, despite the Lebanese army’s presence there.

He challenged officials to “name a single achievement from the seven rounds of negotiations”.

US Ambassador Issa, meanwhile, told reporters Israeli attacks would stop only once Hezbollah disarms.

“If they give up their weapons, everything will stop,” he said.

The June trilateral framework, to which the US is also a party, involves the disarmament of Hezbollah and a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanon’s south, where it has occupied several areas. The gap between the two sides remains wide.

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said on Thursday that Israel will not withdraw until Hezbollah is disarmed, as Israeli forces currently occupy multiple towns inside the Lebanese border.

The Israeli military has continued to occupy Lebanon’s southern area, demolishing homes and displacing residents across the territory.

The next round of talks is expected to resume in early September.

Lebanese authorities say Israel’s attacks since March 2 have killed 4,335 people, wounded 12,277 and displaced more than a million.

articles.title: Vegas Golden Knights unveil quintessentially Sin City center ice design for 10th season
articles.excerpt: The WNBA’s official "task force" met to answer a basic question—what is a woman?—on the heels of Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham taking a stand to protect women's sports and former NBA players En...
articles.body_text:
The WNBA’s official "task force" met to answer a basic question—what is a woman?—on the heels of Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham taking a stand to protect women's sports and former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White declaring for the 2027 WNBA Draft. After failing to reach a conclusion, Commissioner Cathy Engelbert’s league blamed outside "hate and vitriol" and simply scheduled more meetings. On this episode of Don't @ Me, Dan Dakich breaks down the absolute clown show as the WNBA continues to get in its own way.

It's hard to believe, but the Vegas Golden Knights are about to begin their tenth NHL season.

And what a ride it's been. They've gone from the "Golden Misfits" to, at times, embracing their role in many fans' minds as one of the league's premier villainous franchises.

And what better way to celebrate a decade in the NHL than with the most Vegas-y center ice design the league has ever seen?

VEGAS' JACK EICHEL OFFERS A PERFECT RESPONSE TO GOLDEN KNIGHTS BEING VOTED THE MOST-HATED TEAM IN THE NHL

Did we expect anything less from a team that puts on the bastard child of the Ice Capades and Medieval Times before every game?

Personally, I think the design looks great — even if it's almost certainly going to be a nightmare to keep tabs on the puck anytime there's a pass through there — but let's see how the always thoughtful citizens of social media feel about it.

Alright, so maybe your perception depends more on your rooting interests than I had initially thought.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Love 'em or hate 'em, it has been a good nine seasons so far for the Golden Knights, who have already proven themselves to be one of the most successful expansion teams the league has ever seen.

Tomas Hertl of the Golden Knights celebrates a goal against the Anaheim Ducks in this past season's Stanley Cup Playoffs. (Photo by David Becker/NHLI via Getty Images)

They, of course, pulled off a stunner and made it to the Stanley Cup Final in their inaugural campaign back in 2017-18, only to lose to Alex Ovechkin and the Washington Capitals.

In 2023, the team made it back to the Stanley Cup Final; this time they defeated the Florida Panthers for the franchise's first championship.

The Vegas Golden Knights defeated the Florida Panthers to win the Stanley Cup in 2023. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images)

They tried for a second just this season, but lost to the Carolina Hurricanes in six games.

Still, over those nine seasons, three trips to the Cup Final are impressive. But what's more impressive is the consistency the club has shown. They've only missed the playoffs once in their existence, and they still came in fourth in the division that season.

Vegas also continues to be a top choice for a lot of free agents and players asking for trades, so expect the Golden Knights to continue being among the league's perennial contenders.

articles.title: El-Sayed’s half sister offered Oct 7 ‘blessing,’ one year after Hamas attack: ‘Allahu Akbar’
articles.excerpt: Eman Abdelhadi, the half-sister of Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, delivers an "October 7th blessing" one year after the Hamas-led attacks on Israel. (@rabbis4ceasefire via Instag...
articles.body_text:
Eman Abdelhadi, the half-sister of Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, delivers an "October 7th blessing" one year after the Hamas-led attacks on Israel. (@rabbis4ceasefire via Instagram)

University of Chicago professor Eman Abdelhadi, who is the half sister of Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, delivered an "October 7th blessing" one year after Hamas militants killed approximately 1,200 people in widespread terrorist attacks.

"I want to say, Allahu Akbar," Abdelhadi said, opening her blessing in a video posted to Instagram on Oct. 7, 2024. "That phrase means God is greater, and it's an important phrase in the Muslim tradition. It's one that I've been thinking about a lot over the last year, because it's a phrase that reminds us that no matter how great the brutality, the oppression, the intensity of what we're going through. The horizon of justice is just around the corner."

Throughout her video commemorating the anniversary of terrorist attacks, Abdelhadi makes no mention of the Jews killed by Hamas. She filmed her blessing wearing a keffiyeh, a traditional cloth associated with Palestinian militant movements.

"Abdul loves his sister and also disagrees with her on a number of political positions and the rhetoric she's chosen to use, including on foreign policy," a campaign spokeswoman told Fox News Digital when asked about the video. "But Abdul is the one on the ballot and his record of public service and his platform is what matters to voters here in Michigan. His campaign has always been about his love for America and Michigan."

EL-SAYED’S HALF SISTER REVEALED AS RADICAL PROFESSOR ARRESTED FOR ALLEGEDLY ASSAULTING A COP AT ANTI-ICE RIOT

Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks after a radio appearance at Dr. Horace Sheffield's GOTV Community Rally on Aug. 1, 2026, in Detroit, (L) A mugshot of Eman Adbelhadi from Oct. 3, 2025. (Getty Images; Cook County Sheriff's Office)

"There is something greater than even the strongest armies and for me that's God," Abdelhadi continued in the video. "Reflecting on that reaffirms my commitment to justice, my commitment not to get caught up in the narratives that colonial powers enforce on us … I hope you know that we have a lot of work ahead of us and that we need each other to do that work. We have an imperative to not just imagine a better future, but to build one together."

"I’ll see you on the streets," she said, concluding her statement.

The video was posted on Instagram on Oct. 7, 2024, in a collaborative post by "Rabbis4Ceasefire" and Abdelhadi’s account. Rabbis4Ceasefire described it in a caption on the post as an "October 7th blessing from Eman Abdelhadi, Scholar, Writer & Organizer."

In a new comment added Friday, Abdelhadi said Rabbis4Ceasefire had organized and named the event as "a moment of grief for lives lost between 10/7/23 and 10/7/2024," asked her to participate and described the video as her "offering" to the gathering.

The resurfaced video drew sharp criticism on X.

"Jewish Michiganders are proudly putting country over party and rejecting Abdul El-Sayed’s extremism. We must put country over party and elect Mike Rogers," Democrats for Mike Rogers, El-Sayed's GOP challenger, posted in response.

"Abdul El-Sayed's Sister, Eman Abdelhadi, recorded a celebration video in reaction to October 7th," commentator Eyal Yakoby wrote.

Abdelhadi has previously faced legal trouble over her activism, including an October 2025 arrest after she allegedly spat on an Illinois state trooper during protests outside a suburban Chicago ICE detention facility. She was charged with two felony counts of aggravated battery to a government employee and two misdemeanor counts of resisting or obstructing a peace officer.

UNEARTHED EL-SAYED ESSAY DRAWS EXPLOSIVE TRUMP-BIN LADEN PARALLEL

Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks after a radio appearance at Dr. Horace Sheffield's GOTV Community Rally on Aug. 1, 2026, in Detroit, Mich. El-Sayed holds a 15-point lead against Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) according to a recent poll. (Getty Images)

Abdelhadi’s half brother has engendered ample controversy over his statements on the Israel-Palestine conflict while on the campaign trail.

El-Sayed, for instance, sent a fundraising email on the second anniversary of the Oct. 7 terrorist attacks where he criticized the Israeli government’s military operations, but said nothing of Hamas’ initial killings. The Michigan Democrat has equated Hamas and the Israeli government, calling both evil.

ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS RALLYING WITH HASAN PIKER DOESN'T MEAN HE ENDORSES 'AMERICA DESERVED 9/11' REMARK

Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive candidate for U.S. Senate in Michigan, talks poolside with streamer Hasan Piker at a party for content creators supporting his campaign Monday, Aug. 3, 2026, in Detroit. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

He has also received criticism for his continued association and campaign appearances with streamer Hasan Piker, who once said that America "deserved 9/11." Though El-Sayed has called the streamer’s statement "dumb," he has declined to disavow Piker, accusing critics of engaging in cancel culture.

Abdelhadi did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Friday.

articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Six people, including the suspected gunman, are dead in rural Missaukee County, Michigan, following a multi-scene shooting, according to local reports.

Earlier Friday, Michigan State Police shared on social media that officers were investigating a shooting in the area and that authorities were looking for Chad Hickman, 39, who they said should be considered "armed and dangerous."

Police later said that Hickman had been located.

Officers began investigating Friday morning when three people were found dead and another was wounded at a home near LaChance Road and Kelly Road in Richland Township, according to UpNorthLive.

NEW YORK STATE POLICE LAUNCH MANHUNT AFTER KILLING, HOUSE FIRE FOR 'ARMED AND DANGEROUS' SUSPECT

Shooting suspect Chad Hickman was reportedly found dead by police. (Michigan State Police)

A fourth person was reportedly found dead in another home, and a fifth person in a wooded area.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Michigan State Police.

Hickman was later found dead, according to UpNorthLive.

Michigan State Police shared on social media Friday that officers were investigating a shooting in the area and that authorities were looking for the gunman. (Emily Elconin/Getty Images, File)

"Not only is this difficult for our investigators and our troopers, but it's very hard for this community. You know, this type of loss is tragic," MSP Public Information Officer Lt. Ashley Miller told the outlet. "And we're going to conduct a thorough investigation, and we want to make sure to keep our community members up to date on our current situation and what we're discovering throughout this process."

Police haven’t given any more details about what led to the shootings.

Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Yemen’s government says Houthi attack on al-Makha kills at least four
articles.excerpt:
The Houthis have launched an attack on the Red Sea port city of al-Makha (Mocha), killing at least four people, Yemen’s internationally recognised government says.

The government said the Houthis ⁠fi...
articles.body_text:
The Houthis have launched an attack on the Red Sea port city of al-Makha (Mocha), killing at least four people, Yemen’s internationally recognised government says.

The government said the Houthis ⁠fired six ballistic ⁠missiles at al-Makha on Friday, amid an escalation in hostilities between the Iran-aligned group and its Saudi-backed opponents.

The armed forces aligned with the Yemeni government said the attack targeted civilian infrastructure and national assets at the port, adding that initial reports said four civilians were killed and several fishing boats were set on fire.

An unnamed military official from Yemen’s government told the AFP news agency that the strike killed at least eight people, including two security personnel.

The ⁠escalation comes at a time of heightened regional tensions over the US-Israel war on Iran, in which the Houthis have emerged as a key front, raising the prospect of a ⁠return to large-scale conflict in Yemen.

The Houthis said they had attacked what they ‌described as buildups, weapons and warships belonging to Saudi-backed forces and “mercenaries” in al-Makha with a large number of ballistic missiles, destroying boats and weapons.

Separately, the Houthi-run SABA news agency cited a military source as saying the group had targeted an Aramco facility in the Saudi city of Najran with a drone.

The source said the attack was a response to what it described as Saudi military aircraft entering airspace ⁠over the northeastern part of Yemen’s Saada governorate. The report did not ⁠identify the precise target or say whether it had been hit.

There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities or Aramco.

The reported attacks follow a rise in hostilities between the Houthis and Yemen’s internationally recognised government. On Thursday, ⁠the Houthis said they had attacked an Aramco refinery in Saudi Arabia’s Jazan with two drones.

Yemen’s violence comes as US-Iran diplomacy remains stalled.

Iran’s Supreme National Security Council demanded over the weekend that the US end its blockade, lift sanctions, withdraw troops and pay reparations. US President Donald Trump countered by demanding that Iran pay compensation instead, even as Iran and Oman near a deal on a new transit corridor through Hormuz.

articles.title: Kelly Osbourne blasts Dee Snider as 'spectacularly classless' for claiming Ozzy didn’t write his own songs
articles.excerpt:
Piers Morgan remembers Ozzy Osbourne after the heavy metal legend was laid to rest in his hometown of Birmingham, England.

Kelly Osbourne and Twisted Sister frontman Dee Snider are going head-to-head...
articles.body_text:
Piers Morgan remembers Ozzy Osbourne after the heavy metal legend was laid to rest in his hometown of Birmingham, England.

Kelly Osbourne and Twisted Sister frontman Dee Snider are going head-to-head after the retired musician claimed Ozzy Osbourne "always" had other people write his songs for him.

Earlier this week, Snider wrote on X, "Ozzy always had bass players write his lyrics." He went on to claim that bassist Bob Daisley and Motörhead frontman Lemmy Kilmister were frequent writers of Ozzy's music, and that Geezer Butler "wrote ALL of @BlackSabbath lyrics."

According to Daisley's website, he claimed to have written the majority of the songs for Ozzy's first five solo albums. Daisley is credited as a songwriter on "Blizzard of Ozz" and "No Rest for the Wicked." During Ozzy's time with Black Sabbath, Butler was widely credited as the main lyricist for the band.

Snider's comments prompted a sharp response from Ozzy's daughter via her Instagram Stories Friday.

KELLY OSBOURNE DEMANDS CHILD SUPPORT AND HER DOGS BACK IN FIERY RANT AMID REPORTED BREAKUP

Kelly Osbourne called out Dee Snider after he claimed Ozzy Osbourne did not always write his own music. (Getty Images)

Kelly shared two text-heavy posts, including one directly addressing Snider.

"My father’s legacy as a musician, songwriter, singer and bandleader speaks for itself. His friends, those who worked with him, those who love him, and millions of fans around the world that still continue to buy his records know exactly what he meant what he contributed and what he leaves behind. His legacy will live on eternally," Kelly wrote on the first image.

Kelly Osbourne addressed Dee Snider's comments on her Instagram Stories. (Kelly Osbourne/Instagram)

KELLY OSBOURNE WELCOMES FIRST BABY WITH SID WILSON, SHARON OSBOURNE PRAISES DAUGHTER: 'SO PROUD'

In her next Instagram story, Kelly called Snider’s criticism "spectacularly classless" and argued that he had little basis to speak authoritatively about her father's career and legacy.

"And if Snider wants to invite comparisons between their careers, that comparison is devastating enough on its own," she wrote.

Kelly Osbourne called out Dee Snider directly on her Instagram story. (Kelly Osbourne/Instagram)

Kelly then compared Snider and Ozzy's careers, writing, "Snider had a brief period of mainstream success more than 40 years ago. My father's career spanned nearly six decades — from helping define heavy metal with Black Sabbath to building an extraordinary solo career. His music will continue influencing generations long after all of us are gone."

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Kelly suggested that Snider’s criticism was an attempt to put himself back into the conversation, while her father’s "name, catalogue and influence" remain globally relevant. She argued that Ozzy’s accomplishments stand on their own, writing, "My father doesn’t need Dee Snider’s approval to establish his place in music history."

Kelly Osbourne fiercely protected her late father, Ozzy Osbourne's, legacy. (Kevin Mazur)

She concluded, "trying to make my father smaller won’t make Dee Snider bigger," arguing that attacking Ozzy’s legacy only draws greater attention to the difference between the two musicians’ careers and lasting cultural impact.

Early Friday morning, Snider returned to X to make it clear that he has "nothing but love for Ozzy."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"He was always lovely to me. @BlackSabbath changed my life! As a songwriter I can be a little touchy about credit and royalties," Snider wrote.

Dee Snider clarified that he has "nothing but love" for Ozzy Osbourne. (Scott Dudelson/Getty Images)

Representatives for Kelly did not respond to Fox News Digital. Snider's representative said the rocker had no further comment.

Ozzy died on July 22, 2025, at 76, just weeks after performing his final concert with Black Sabbath. His death certificate later listed cardiac arrest and coronary artery disease among the causes of his death, with Parkinson’s disease noted as a contributing condition.

Janelle Ash is an entertainment writer for Fox News Digital covering Hollywood, celebrity culture and breaking entertainment news through exclusive reporting, interviews and in-depth storytelling.

articles.title: Butch Huskey, one of the last MLB players to wear Jackie Robinson's famed number 42, dies at 54
articles.excerpt: In 1947, Jackie Robinson broke Major League Baseball’s color barrier, becoming the first African American player in the modern era. He went on to win Rookie of the Year in 1947 and was inducted into t...
articles.body_text:
In 1947, Jackie Robinson broke Major League Baseball’s color barrier, becoming the first African American player in the modern era. He went on to win Rookie of the Year in 1947 and was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1962.

Butch Huskey, one of the final MLB players to wear No. 42, has died at age 54.

Huskey initially wore No. 10 with the New York Mets but changed his jersey number to No. 42 in 1995, two years before Major League Baseball retired the number league-wide in honor of Jackie Robinson.

Yet when MLB retired the number, it allowed those already wearing it — like Huskey, Mo Vaughn and Mariano Rivera — to be grandfathered in and continue donning the number on their jerseys as long as they were still playing, no matter who they played for.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Brian McRae of the New York Mets is congratulated by teammate Butch Huskey as he crosses home plate to score on a single by teammate Alberto Castillo as Matt Franco runs from the dugout on March 31 at Shea Stadium in Flushing, New York. The Mets beat the Philadelphia Phillies 1-0 after 15 innings in their home opener. (Jon Levy/AFP via Getty Images)

Thus, even when Huskey left the Mets, he was able to wear the number with the Seattle Mariners and Minnesota Twins. Huskey also played for the Boston Red Sox in 1999 but opted for No. 44.

The Mets announced his death on social media.

Huskey made his MLB debut in 1993 but did not get full playing time until three years later with his new number. Playing mostly first base in 1996, he impressed with a .278 batting average and .754 OPS. In 1997, he improved by hitting .287 with an .822 OPS, belting a career-high 24 home runs and driving in 81 runs, also the most of his career. He took a step back the following season, though, and was traded to the Mariners the following offseason.

Outfielder Butch Huskey of the New York Mets is in action during a game against the Houston Astros at Shea Stadium in Flushing, New York, on April 27, 1998. The Mets defeated the Astros 4-3. (David Seelig/Getty Images)

ANTHONY VOLPE HAS FACE-PALM MOMENT WITH ABS SYSTEM AS FIRST BATTER OF MINOR LEAGUE GAME

Huskey was then moved from Seattle to Boston in the 1999 season. The Sox made the postseason as a wild card, but they lost to the New York Yankees in the American League Championship Series en route to the Bombers' second of three straight World Series victories.

His last stint was with the Colorado Rockies, with whom he wore No. 35.

Huskey is the last person to wear No. 42 in Mariners history, and only four players wore it after him in the big leagues: Vaughn, Rivera, Michael Jackson and Jose Lima.

A view from behind home plate displays the art on the field in memory of Jackie Robinson during the Los Angeles Dodgers' 5-2 win over the New York Mets at Shea Stadium in Flushing, New York, on April 16, 1997. Butch Huskey of the New York Mets is the batter. (Getty Images)

The number was retired for Robinson during one of Huskey's Mets games against Robinson's former Dodgers, who had since moved to Los Angeles.

Follow Fox News Digital’s sports coverage on X, and subscribe to the Fox News Sports Huddle newsletter.

articles.title: Trump leaves stage mid-speech to embrace parents of 12-year-old killed by stray bullet in the Bronx
articles.excerpt: President Donald Trump exits the stage to the parents of Jacob Freytes, a Bronx boy who was killed by a repeat criminal's stray bullet. Trump was on Long Island, N.Y., Friday addressing law enforcemen...
articles.body_text:
President Donald Trump exits the stage to the parents of Jacob Freytes, a Bronx boy who was killed by a repeat criminal's stray bullet. Trump was on Long Island, N.Y., Friday addressing law enforcement about his administration's crackdown on crime.

President Donald Trump stepped off the stage on Friday while making a speech in New York to comfort the family of a 12-year-old boy who was killed by a stray bullet in the Bronx.

Trump was speaking to the Nassau County Police Academy when he mentioned Jacob Freytes, a boy who was killed late last month by a stray bullet while sitting on his bike outside a bodega.

"In a beautiful impromptu moment, President Trump exits the stage in the middle of his speech to embrace Migdalia Martinez and retired NYPD Sergeant Jesus Freytes, whose 12-year-old son Jacob was tragically killed by a stray bullet in the Bronx," White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt wrote on social media after capturing the moment on video.

CRIME IS FALLING, OFFICIALS SAY — VICTIMS CLAIM REPORTING ISN’T WORTH IT

President Donald Trump stepped off the stage on Friday while making a speech on Long Island, N.Y., to comfort the family of a 12-year-old boy who was killed by a stray bullet in the Bronx. (Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty Images)

Before leaving the stage to meet his parents, Trump mentioned Freytes while talking about his administration’s effort to lower crime.

"Two weeks ago, a 12-year-old boy named Jacob Freytes — You read about this one? — was tragically shot and killed by a stray bullet fired by a repeat offender in a gun battle."

He added: "Jacob was the son of a loving mom and a retired New York City police detective, and they are incredible people, and I think I heard that they may be with us today. Are you with us?"

Migdalia Martinez and retired NYPD Sgt. Jesus Freytas watch President Trump speak about their son Friday in Garden City, N.Y. (Getty Images)

He then left the stage and hugged Freytes' teary-eyed mom, Migdalia Martinez, and his father, retired NYPD Sgt. Jesus Freytes, saying a few private words to both of them.

AS SOCIALIST MAYOR BATTLES ICE, SEATTLE POLICE AND CRIME VICTIMS SAY REPEAT OFFENDERS ARE TERRORIZING THE CITY

"Incredible. Horrible story. What a horrible thing," he said when he returned to the stage. "But we're going after them. These are bad, sick people."

President Donald Trump speaks at the Nassau County Policy Academy David S. Mack Center for Training and Intelligence in Garden City, N.Y., on Friday. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Freytes’ death has prompted Republicans to introduce "Jacob’s Law" in the New York Legislature that would put harsher penalties on criminals whose reckless actions result in the death of a child.

"I gave him a kiss, and I walked out, and we always do a little dolphin kiss. And I walked out and went to work," Martinez told "Fox & Friends" Tuesday.

"Around five o'clock, they called me and said that he had gotten shot. And all I could do was try to think of different ways to get here faster," she added. "When I got there, I just seen my boy gone."

Police said William Ferrer, 45, was arrested and faces multiple charges, including second-degree murder. He has pleaded not guilty. Ferrer has an arrest record dating back more than 25 years, including prior charges for drunk driving, drug possession, menacing and criminal contempt, according to the New York Post.

Fox News' Madison Colombo contributed to this report.

Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: FBI captures Top Ten Most Wanted fugitive with alleged Sinaloa Cartel ties, Patel says
articles.excerpt:
Los Angeles Police Department Chief Jim McDonnell says authorities are now offering a $1 million reward for Omar Alexander Cardenas, a suspect on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list. (KTTV)

The ...
articles.body_text:
Los Angeles Police Department Chief Jim McDonnell says authorities are now offering a $1 million reward for Omar Alexander Cardenas, a suspect on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list. (KTTV)

The FBI captured Ten Most Wanted fugitive Gregory Henderson Jr., just three days after adding the alleged Indianapolis gang leader to its list and offering a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest.

Henderson, 46, had evaded arrest since a sweeping federal takedown of his alleged organization in August 2023. He faces federal charges of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute and to distribute controlled substances, conspiracy to launder monetary instruments and conspiracy to engage in an animal fighting venture.

The FBI alleges Henderson led a violent Indianapolis gang whose drug trafficking network was supplied by the Sinaloa Cartel and distributed methamphetamine, cocaine and fentanyl throughout Indianapolis and the surrounding Midwest.

WOMAN ADDED TO FBI'S TEN MOST WANTED LIST ARRESTED HOURS LATER AFTER TIPS POURED IN FROM FLORIDA: PATEL

The FBI marked Gregory Henderson Jr.’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives poster "CAPTURED" following his arrest. (FBI)

His capture marks the ninth FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive apprehended since President Donald Trump returned to office. The nine fugitives had collectively spent more than 50 years on the run, according to the FBI. The FBI says the nine captures are more than twice the four Ten Most Wanted fugitives captured during the Biden administration.

FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital exclusively that Henderson’s capture reflected a broader increase in Ten Most Wanted apprehensions under the Trump administration.

"Nine Top Ten Most Wanted Fugitives is more than twice as many as captured under the entirety of the prior administration — and this FBI and our partners did it in 18 months under President Trump’s brilliant leadership," Patel said. "Gregory Henderson Jr. had been on the run for a year, wanted for his alleged involvement in major drug trafficking operation and animal fighting conspiracies as the alleged leader of a violent neighborhood-based gang located in Indianapolis, Indiana - a gang with significant drug distribution ties to the Sinaloa Cartel."

"This administration is letting good cops be cops and they are delivering in historic ways. I’d like to congratulate our FBI Indianapolis team who led this case from the beginning and thank our great Justice Department and law enforcement partners who righteously pursued this case with us," he added.

'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN

Gregory Henderson Jr. was captured after being added to the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list on Aug. 11. (FBI)

The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Office of Inspector General was among the federal partners involved in the case.

"I would like to thank the FBI, DOJ, and our USDA OIG among many other federal partners in their relentless pursuit for justice. Mr. Henderson had sought to evade the law after committing multiple crimes and leaving behind pain and anguish for many people and animals, but today is the end of that devastation," U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins told Fox News Digital "President Trump has focused his administration on delivering justice for those targeted by violent crimes, and we will not rest until we achieve this goal."

The FBI added Henderson to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list on Aug. 11, describing him as armed and dangerous.

Henderson and 20 others were federally indicted in the Southern District of Indiana in August 2023 on drug trafficking and dog fighting conspiracy charges. More than 300 federal, state and local law enforcement officers carried out a takedown later that month, arresting 18 people while Henderson evaded capture.

Federal agents seized 61 guns, quantities of fentanyl, methamphetamine and cocaine, $98,000 in cash and 166 fighting dogs during the operation, according to the FBI.

Law enforcement also uncovered what the FBI described as a significant dog fighting and illegal gambling operation allegedly led by Henderson.

"Henderson Jr. has a long history of criminal activity, including street violence, intimidation, assault, and weapons, in addition to drug trafficking and animal cruelty," said FBI Indianapolis Special Agent in Charge Tim O’Malley.

Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel (C) speaks at a news conference at the Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice building on June 23, 2026, in Washington, DC. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Details about where and how Henderson was captured were not immediately available.

Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

articles.title: Trump downplays concerns about sailors onboard USS Abraham Lincoln amid record deployment
articles.excerpt:
President said nine months at sea ‘not nearly long enough’ even as families call for attention to mental health crisis

Donald Trump has downplayed concerns about US sailors enduring a record-setting ...
articles.body_text:
President said nine months at sea ‘not nearly long enough’ even as families call for attention to mental health crisis

Donald Trump has downplayed concerns about US sailors enduring a record-setting deployment of nearly nine months onboard the USS Abraham Lincoln on Friday, saying the deployment was “not nearly long enough” as concerns mount over mental health and supply issues onboard the aircraft carrier.

The US president made the comments during a brief exchange with reporters before flying to New York for an event highlighting falling violent crime rates across the US.

“That ship is moving right now, or very shortly, and it’s being replaced with another very similar ship,” Trump said when asked about the lengthy deployment. When asked by reporters whether family members were worried about the situation, the president claimed: “No, they’re not.”

The Lincoln has been supporting the US war against Iran, and several Democratic lawmakers are pressing the Pentagon for accountability over conditions onboard the carrier. The defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, on Thursday said those conditions had been “completely misrepresented”.

Military families and US Congress members have called attention to the intensifying mental health crisis for those onboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, as its 5,000 sailors and marines endure a record-breaking deployment at sea tied to the war with Iran.

The scrutiny comes as the navy has reimposed a blockade on Iranian ports in the crucial strait of Hormuz, even as hostilities between the US and Iran have calmed in recent weeks. The Trump administration has offered no clarity on how it intends to wind down the war, while Hegseth has suggested the US military can maintain the blockage of Iranian ports “indefinitely”.

Another aircraft carrier, the USS George Washington, left port in Da Nang, Vietnam, last week and is expected to replace the Lincoln, one of two aircraft carriers currently deployed in the Middle East.

Two leading specialist military papers, the Navy Times and Stars and Stripes, reported that there have been multiple attempts by sailors to jump overboard as poor conditions and mental stresses on the Lincoln reach a breaking point in its ninth month at sea.

One sailor succeeded in early August, a US official confirmed. “The sailor was quickly recovered by an air wing search and rescue helicopter, treated by Abraham Lincoln’s medical department, and transferred off ship for follow-on care.”

Worried families expressed their concerns about loved ones onboard the Lincoln at an emotional town hall meeting with navy leaders in San Diego last week, Stars and Stripes reported. One spouse among the 200 or so family members said that her husband had texted her that day saying “he hopes he doesn’t wake up tomorrow”.

The US navy said it has “not observed an increase in suicidal ideations or attempts aboard the ship”, but declined to provide data, citing operational security and patient privacy concerns.

The Lincoln is “operating in a highly contested environment where traditional supply hubs in the Middle East were disrupted by combat actions”, the US official said, adding that navy leaders had “prioritized mission-critical supplies: first food, then hygiene items, then mail”.

“Current reports from the ship confirm continuous access to clean water, functional [air conditioning], and healthy meal options,” the official claimed.

In a statement released on Friday, Hung Cao, the acting secretary of the navy, similarly downplayed the reports, saying that “sailors and marines are expected to dig deep” and accused the media of “trying to paint our warriors as victims”.

The statement acknowledged that a “small number” of mental health cases were “treated with no loss of life”, and added that “there is no question our young men and women have been pushed to their limits”.

articles.title: Air Force athletes chasing Olympic dreams in between serving the nation in a critical time
articles.excerpt:
Chad Senior, Texas Tanner and Anita Alvarez talk to Fox News Digital about what its like being an elite athlete while also serving in the U.S. Air Force.

As U.S. airmen carry out combat operations in...
articles.body_text:
Chad Senior, Texas Tanner and Anita Alvarez talk to Fox News Digital about what its like being an elite athlete while also serving in the U.S. Air Force.

As U.S. airmen carry out combat operations in the war with Iran, a small group of service members is representing the Air Force in a different arena: elite international sports.

Through the World Class Athlete Program, or WCAP, Air Force athletes can train full time while remaining on active duty. Their assignment is to compete at the highest level, promote the service and attempt to qualify for the Olympic Games. When their athletic careers end, they return to conventional military roles.

The program’s mission has taken on added weight since U.S. Central Command launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran on Feb. 28. An April 6 CENTCOM fact sheet said American forces had struck more than 13,000 targets using bombers, fighters, tankers, surveillance aircraft, electronic-warfare platforms and airlifters. The conflict remained unresolved in August.

TRUMP HONORS TWO RECORD-BREAKING ATHLETES AT US COAST GUARD ACADEMY GRADUATION CEREMONY

Against that backdrop, Airman First Class Anita Alvarez, 2nd Lt. Texas Tanner and 1st Lt. Wyatt Hendrickson are training toward the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Retired Air Force combat rescue officer Chad Senior offers an example of how an elite athlete’s experience can eventually translate into operational military service.

A view of Anita Alvarez at Maria Lenk Aquatics Centre in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Getty Images)

Their circumstances are not identical. Alvarez and Senior are Olympians, although Senior competed through the Army’s athlete program before joining the Air Force. Tanner and Hendrickson have not yet reached the Olympics, but both have won major national championships while serving.

Alvarez entered the Air Force as an established Olympic medalist. She had already competed in three Olympic Games and helped the United States win the artistic-swimming team silver medal in Paris in 2024.

She entered Basic Military Training in November 2024 and graduated at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland in January 2025. According to the Air Force, she became the first Olympic medalist specifically recruited into the Department of the Air Force’s WCAP program.

The Air Force did not produce her Olympic medal, but it has helped extend her career. Before enlisting, Alvarez said she balanced eight-hour training days with side jobs, school and uncertainty about what she would do after leaving her sport. WCAP allowed her to make training, recovery and mental preparation her full-time job.

"I can put everything not only into the physical training every day, but also into my mental performance, into my recovery," Alvarez said.

Her results since joining the service suggest the arrangement is working. World Aquatics records show that Alvarez won two World Cup bronze medals in team events in 2025. In 2026, she added a team acrobatic gold medal in Medellin, three silver medals in team and duet events, and two more bronze medals.

Alvarez is also completing her degree while considering a post-athletic Air Force career. She expressed interest in aerospace physiology, becoming an officer and possibly pursuing pilot training.

Listening to other airmen discuss deployments and operational missions has also changed how she views her athletic assignment.

"I’m grateful for the opportunities to be able to compete and travel and do all these things in my sport because of the military members and what they’re doing overseas," Alvarez said.

Tanner’s rise came through the Air Force Academy. The Sheridan, Wyoming, native completed one of the strongest throwing careers in Academy history before graduating and receiving his commission in 2026.

TRUMP WARNS US 'WON'T HAVE MUCH OF AN OLYMPIC TEAM ANYMORE' WITHOUT NEW COLLEGE SPORTS REGULATIONS

During his final collegiate season, Tanner set American collegiate records in both the discus and hammer. He finished second in the hammer and fourth in the discus at the NCAA outdoor championships, ending his Academy career as a six-time All-American.

Only weeks after commissioning, Tanner won his first senior national championship. He threw 65.46 meters to capture the U.S. discus title in New York on July 25, winning by nearly a meter and a half. Two days earlier, he placed sixth in the hammer with a throw of 71.64 meters.

The performance moved Tanner closer to his goal of competing at the Los Angeles Games.

"It was to be a national champion," Tanner said. "Now that I’ve accomplished that, it’s to be the best in the world."

Tanner said military service is part of a family tradition that includes his father, aunt, uncle, cousin and grandfather. He did not enter the Academy expecting to become a professional athlete, but WCAP opened that path after he had already committed to military service.

When his throwing career ends, Tanner expects to enter Air Force contracting, helping acquire the goods and services needed to operate aircraft, installations and military units.

"To be able to serve my country in more ways than one is honestly just something that is a legacy through my family," Tanner said.

Hendrickson has produced one of WCAP’s most visible recent achievements. After graduating from the Air Force Academy in 2024, he used his final season of college eligibility at Oklahoma State while serving on active duty through the program.

Shamil Magomed A Sharipov of Bahrain competes against Wyatt Avery Hendrickson of the United States during the UWW Grand Prix Ranking Series Zagreb Open 2026 men's freestyle 125-kilogram gold medal match in Zagreb, Croatia, on Feb. 5, 2026. (Xinhua News Agency via Getty Images)

In March 2025, Hendrickson defeated Olympic champion Gable Steveson to win the NCAA heavyweight wrestling championship. He finished the season undefeated and received the Dan Hodge Trophy as the nation’s outstanding college wrestler.

Hendrickson then won the 2025 Pan American championship and earned a place on the U.S. senior world team. He placed 17th at that year’s World Championships before returning in 2026 to win another Pan American title.

In June, Hendrickson defeated world medalist Mason Parris in two consecutive matches at Final X, securing the 125-kilogram position on the U.S. world team for the second straight year.

"If this were an Olympic year, I’d be an Olympian," Hendrickson said.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

His long-term goal is an Olympic gold medal in Los Angeles. He said WCAP provides the command support and resources that make it possible for him to continue wrestling while remaining an active-duty officer.

"If it weren’t for WCAP, I would not be a wrestler today," Hendrickson said. "They are really the backbone of support while I’m trying to pursue an Olympic gold medal."

Hendrickson also acknowledged that other airmen are performing operational work he otherwise might be doing. After wrestling, he expects to serve as an acquisitions officer responsible for obtaining equipment and other resources for the Air Force.

"I really have to give more credit to the airmen that are kind of filling my role right now," he said. "Hopefully I can repay them by bringing back a gold medal for the United States of America."

Senior’s career shows what that transition from international competition to military operations can look like.

Senior competed in modern pentathlon through the Army’s World Class Athlete Program. He entered the 2000 Olympic year ranked No. 1 in the world, finished sixth at the Sydney Games and placed 13th at the 2004 Athens Olympics.

After the Sept. 11 attacks, Senior decided to leave elite competition and move into a more operational military role. He became an Air Force combat rescue officer and served with the 920th Rescue Wing and 308th Rescue Squadron.

Air Force and Army records credit him with two deployments to Afghanistan and one to Iraq. He later became the 308th Rescue Squadron’s director of operations and rose to the rank of lieutenant colonel before retiring.

Senior now works as a contractor supporting the Air Force and helping plan contingency rescues for human-spaceflight crews.

He argues that WCAP’s value cannot be measured only by medals. Elite athletes arrive with years of experience in discipline, teamwork, failure and high-pressure performance. Those qualities, he said, can later strengthen operational military units.

A U.S. Air Force F-15 Eagle performs during a demonstration flight in Miami, Florida, on May 25. (Jesus Olarte/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Senior views the program as an investment serving three groups: athletes receive the opportunity to pursue world-class goals, the military gains future service members and recruiting ambassadors, and taxpayers gain personnel accustomed to performing under stress.

The real return, he said, comes after athletes leave competition and bring those habits back to the military.

For Alvarez, Tanner and Hendrickson, that test remains ahead. Their present assignment is not combat service, and none claimed that winning a medal was equivalent to carrying out a military mission.

Instead, they described their athletic careers as another form of representation—and as preparation for the work they will eventually perform outside the pool, throwing circle or wrestling arena.

Alvarez is pursuing a fourth Olympic appearance. Tanner is a national champion only months after receiving his commission. Hendrickson has earned consecutive positions on the U.S. world team.

Their immediate objective is Los Angeles. The Air Force’s longer wager is that the discipline required to reach the Olympics will remain valuable after the competition ends and a different kind of service begins.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

articles.title: Luigi Mangione admits shooting healthcare CEO Brian Thompson and pleads guilty on federal charges – live
articles.excerpt:
Defense team file motion to dismiss state murder case on double jeopardy rules after Mangione tells Manhattan court ‘I shot Mr Thompson and he died’

Full report: Mangione pleads guilty to federal sta...
articles.body_text:
Defense team file motion to dismiss state murder case on double jeopardy rules after Mangione tells Manhattan court ‘I shot Mr Thompson and he died’

Full report: Mangione pleads guilty to federal stalking charges

Luigi Mangione has pleaded guilty to federal stalking charges in the 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, telling the judge: “I shot Mr Thompson in Manhattan and he died.”

Mangione said that “after years of enduring severe back pain, a broken back, navigating the obstacles of the health system,” he learned that UnitedHealthcare would be holding it’s annual investor convergence in December 2024. The location was not public but he traveled to New York City and emailed UnitedHealthcare leadership, posing as an institutional investor, to get more information, getting a response within an hour.

He also researched who would be attending. Mangione then said he printed a gun with a 3-D printer and affixed it with a silencer. “I shot Mr Thompson in Manhattan and he died,” he continued. “When I did so, I understood that my actions would place him in fear of death or serious bodily injury. I knew what I was doing was illegal.”

Judge Margaret Garnett accepted the plea and will sentence Mangione on 18 December. Mangione’s lawyer also confirmed to the judge that there is no plea agreement with the government. He will remain in federal custody as he awaits sentencing. He faces life in prison.

Mangione, 28, entered the plea at a hastily scheduled hearing in Manhattan federal court this morning, resolving one of two cases against him in connection with Thompson’s killing. With this guilty plea, his lawyers could seek to have the state case – for which he has pleaded not guilty to murder and is scheduled to go on trial next month – thrown out on double jeopardy grounds.

Brian Thompson’s family called the plea “an important step toward justice”. “Now we look to the court to ensure that sentencing reflects the severity of this crime,” the family said in a statement. “We remain mindful that additional proceedings in New York and Pennsylvania are still to come, and we will continue to seek the justice Brian deserves.

Meanwhile, Luigi Mangione’s defense team filed a motion to have the state murder case dismissed on double jeopardy grounds, one of his attorney’s, Karen Friedman Agnifilo, told reporters outside the courthouse. She said Mangione had been “unfairly treated since the outset” and was “being prosecuted twice for the same conduct”. “Today’s guilty plea triggers [New York’s state’s double jeopardy] statue and we just filed our motion in state court explaining why the state charges must be dismissed under the state’s double jeopardy protections,” she said.

The Manhattan District Attorney’s Office said, “We are encouraged that Mr. Thompson’s family received a measure of accountability today.” It added that it is “prepared to litigate the defense motions”.

Jamie McDonald, the US attorney for the southern district of New York, told reporters that his office does not have a plea agreement with Mangione and said that it would seek the maximum sentence of life in prison. He added that “there can be no celebrity in assassination”, and that “any person who celebrates, encourages or excuses actions like these is fundamentally wrong ... Violence is not a legitimate instrument to promote any political or social message.”

UnitedHealth Group - UnitedHealthcare’s parent company - said: “Brian Thompson’s life was cut short by an act of violence that devastated everyone who knew and loved him. We are grateful to law enforcement for bringing Brian’s murderer to justice, and our thoughts remain with Brian’s family and loved ones during this difficult time.”

UnitedHealth Group - UnitedHealthcare’s parent company - has issued this statement.

double quotation markBrian Thompson’s life was cut short by an act of violence that devastated everyone who knew and loved him. We are grateful to law enforcement for bringing Brian’s murderer to justice, and our thoughts remain with Brian’s family and loved ones during this difficult time.

Jamie McDonald, the US attorney for the southern district of New York, told reporters that his office does not have a plea agreement with Mangione and said that it would seek the maximum sentence of life in prison.

double quotation markNow [Mangione] stands convicted in federal court and faces life in prison … While the defendant pleaded guilty, our office does not have a plea agreement with him. Instead, he pleaded open, which means he pleaded guilty to all pending counts in the indictment. There are no accommodations or concessions, and we are free to seek the maximum penalty under the law … The results achieved today now allow our office to seek the maximum penalty allowed — life imprisonment.

McDonald also said, “There can be no celebrity in assassination.”

“Any person who celebrates, encourages or excuses actions like these is fundamentally wrong,” he said. “Violence is not a legitimate instrument to promote any political or social message.”

The Manhattan District Attorney’s Office released this statement.

double quotation markSince December 2024, the Manhattan D.A.’s Office has been tirelessly preparing to pursue a trial conviction in New York State Supreme Court for the alleged cold-blooded murder of Brian Thompson. We are encouraged that Mr. Thompson’s family received a measure of accountability today.

While federal sentencing is pending, we are prepared to litigate the defense motions. The Manhattan D.A.’s Office remains committed to seeking justice for Mr. Thompson and his family.

Also speaking outside the courthouse following the guilty plea, NYPD commissioner Jessica Tisch hailed this as “an important moment of accountability” in Brian Thompson’s killing.

“My thoughts remain first and foremost with Mr. Thompson’s family and everyone who knew and loved him,” she said, and also commended the “extraordinary police work that brought us here”.

She ended her statement with this message:

double quotation markAnd to those who idolize Luigi Mangione, I say this: Violence is not a cause. Murder is not a message, and a killer is certainly not a hero.

Following Luigi Mangione’s guilty plea in the federal case against him, his defense team has just filed a motion in state court, triggering double jeopardy to dismiss the state murder case, one of his attorney’s Karen Friedman Agnifilo told reporters outside the courthouse. The state trial is set for 8 September.

Here are Friedman Agnifilo’s full comments:

double quotation markWith today’s guilty plea, Mr Mangione has accepted full responsibility for the death of Brian Thompson.

It was a single tragic event, yet he’s being prosecuted twice for the same conduct.

As Luigi explained in court today, he endured years of severe, debilitating pain following a broken back, while struggling to navigate our healthcare and health insurance systems.

Like the thousands of people who have reached out since this tragedy to share their own experiences, he believed that the system had failed him and destroyed his life.

Despite this being a single isolated event, Mr Mangione has been unfairly treated since the outset in every way, and have successfully fought off terrorism charges and the death penalty, while also fighting at the same time two simultaneous prosecutions in two jurisdictions, who are punish him twice for the exact conduct.

He’s been treated differently from every other defendant charged with this offence in New York. However, thankfully, New York law does not … permit a person to be prosecuted and punished twice for the exact same crime ... It’s also known as the double jeopardy law.

Today’s guilty plea triggers this statue and we just filed our motion in state court explaining why the state charges must be dismissed under the state’s double jeopardy protections.

Brian Thompson’s family has issued this statement.

double quotation markToday’s guilty plea marks an important step toward justice for Brian and for our family. While nothing will ease the pain of losing him, we are grateful that the federal justice system has held the person responsible for this heinous act accountable. Now we look to the court to ensure that sentencing reflects the severity of this crime. We remain mindful that additional proceedings in New York and Pennsylvania are still to come, and we will continue to seek the justice Brian deserves.

He also researched who would be attending. Mangione then said he printed a gun with a 3-D printer and affixed it with a silencer. “I shot Mr Thompson in Manhattan and he died,” he continued. “When I did so, I understood that my actions would place him in fear of death or serious bodily injury. I knew what I was doing was illegal.”
